name: IGF-1

card.summary: The growth hormone-driven hormone that builds muscle, bone and cartilage, which is why height, jaw and physique communities track it and try to raise it through diet, training and sleep.
card.aka: insulin-like growth factor 1, somatomedin C; mecasermin (rhIGF-1); IGF-1 LR3
card.note: Recombinant IGF-1 is prescription-only for severe deficiency; levels that are too high or too low are both linked to health risks.

quick.overview:
IGF-1 is a hormone made mainly in the liver in response to growth hormone. It acts on nearly every cell type, especially skeletal muscle, cartilage, bone and nerve cells, and mediates many of growth hormone's effects. Levels peak in puberty and decline after about the third decade.

For appearance it is the link between growth hormone and body size: height, bone development and muscle mass. In looksmaxxing forums, "IGF-1 signaling" is discussed as something to support with diet and lifestyle, and synthetic forms such as IGF-1 LR3 appear in peptide discussions.
quick.how: People mostly talk about nutrition, sleep and training choices said to influence IGF-1, for example protein intake, which Wikipedia notes raises IGF-1. Recombinant IGF-1 (mecasermin) is a prescription medicine used under specialist care for children with severe IGF-1 deficiency. Research-peptide forms are discussed in communities but are not approved products.
quick.risks: Wikipedia reports that both high and low IGF-1 levels are linked to higher mortality, with mid-range levels linked to the lowest risk; high levels are associated with some cancers. Recombinant IGF-1 can cause low blood sugar and is regulated. Unapproved peptide forms carry unknown purity and dosing risks.

lead: Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1, also called somatomedin C) is a hormone similar in structure to insulin. It is made mainly in the liver in response to growth hormone (GH) and acts on nearly every cell type, especially skeletal muscle, cartilage, bone and nerve cells. Wikipedia reports that the GH and IGF-1 axis contributes to muscle strength, muscle mass and skeletal development, and that levels peak during puberty [1]. It is described as the main mediator of GH's growth effects [2].

Appearance communities care about it for height, bone structure and muscle. A review of skeletal muscle describes IGF-1 as a key growth factor that increases muscle protein synthesis through PI3K/Akt/mTOR signalling and suppresses muscle breakdown pathways [3]. Looksmax.org threads discuss "IGF-1 signaling" in relation to diet, bone growth and the mandible, alongside sceptical posters who ask whether it is a coping mechanism [4][5][6].

Recombinant IGF-1, mecasermin (brand name Increlex), is used medically for growth failure in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency and is the main treatment for Laron syndrome, in which patients do not respond to growth hormone [1][7][8]. Other synthetic variants, such as IGF-1 LR3, are sold as research chemicals and are discussed in peptide and bodybuilding forums.

chain: IGF-1 drives cartilage, bone and muscle growth
angle.text: IGF-1 is the signal through which growth hormone builds bone, cartilage and muscle. Community interest centres on supporting it through lifestyle during growth years and on peptide forms.

paras: IGF-1 is a single chain of 70 amino acids held in shape by three disulfide bridges, with a molecular weight of about 7.6 kDa; it is encoded by the IGF1 gene on chromosome 12 [1]. Its two main structural domains resemble the A and B chains of proinsulin, which explains the name and its ability to bind the insulin receptor as well as its own receptor, IGF-1R [1][9]. Grokipedia adds that roughly three quarters of circulating IGF-1 comes from the liver, with muscle, bone and brain producing it locally for nearby effects [9].

Most circulating IGF-1 travels bound to one of six IGF binding proteins (IGFBP-1 to IGFBP-6), which govern how much is available to tissues; IGFBP-1 is regulated by insulin [1]. A splice variant called mechano growth factor (MGF) shares the mature region but has a different E domain [1].

Growth hormone stimulates the liver to release IGF-1, and IGF-1 in turn feeds back to suppress GH release from the pituitary and hypothalamus [2]. GH also acts directly on tissues such as cartilage cells, so IGF-1 is the main but not the only route of GH's effects [2]. Binding to IGF-1R triggers intracellular signalling, notably the Akt pathway, which promotes cell growth and proliferation and inhibits programmed cell death [1].

Levels peak during puberty, fall sharply after the third decade and keep declining gradually until about the eighth decade [1]. In mice, IGF-1 deficiency reduced body and tissue mass while excess expression increased it [1].

In skeletal muscle, a 2020 review in Cells describes IGF-1 as raising protein synthesis through PI3K/Akt/mTOR and GSK3 beta pathways, and as inhibiting FoxO transcription factors that drive protein breakdown; it may also dampen myostatin and inflammatory signalling that promote atrophy [3]. A 2025 review discusses IGF-1 as a growth factor under study for tendon regeneration [10].

In 1957 Salmon and Daughaday reported a serum factor, dependent on growth hormone, that stimulated sulfate uptake into cartilage in vitro; it became known as the sulfation factor [1]. In the 1970s a separate activity was characterised as nonsuppressible insulin-like activity (NSILA) [1]. Work in the late 1970s established that these were related molecules: Rinderknecht and Humbel published the amino acid sequence in 1978, the cDNA sequence followed in 1983 and the gene was mapped to chromosome 12 in 1985 [1]. The name somatomedin C gave way to insulin-like growth factor 1 [1].

The clinical story runs through Laron syndrome. Israeli paediatric endocrinologist Zvi Laron and colleagues described children in 1966 who were very short but had high growth hormone; later work showed IGF-1 failed to rise when GH was given, pointing to a defect in the GH receptor [8]. Recombinant IGF-1 became a treatment for this group, and the FDA approved mecasermin products in 2005 [8].

Interest is in height, jaw and bone mass and muscle. For height, the relevant window is childhood and puberty, when IGF-1 peaks and growth plates are open [1]. For physique, IGF-1 appears in discussions of muscle growth, recovery and tendon health [3][10]. Dietary research links IGF-1 with acne through glycemic load and dairy intake, though a systematic review found the dairy literature mixed [11].

Because GH and IGF-1 are the pathways clinics target for short stature and body composition, community members who cannot or will not use prescription GH sometimes look to diet, sleep, training and peptides that they say influence IGF-1 [4][12].

Mecasermin is indicated for long-term treatment of growth failure in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, including GH insensitivity such as Laron syndrome; it is given by subcutaneous injection [7]. It has also been explored in other conditions such as diabetes and anorexia nervosa [7]. A related product, mecasermin rinfabate (Iplex), combined mecasermin with IGFBP-3 to prolong its action [7].

IGF-1 is also a diagnostic marker. Clinicians use it with the IGF-1 to IGFBP-3 ratio when evaluating GH deficiency, acromegaly and gigantism [1]. It is among the hormones reviewed in the sports-doping literature, where peptide hormones and growth factors are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency [13]. Trofinetide, approved in the US in 2023 for Rett syndrome, is a synthetic analogue of glycine-proline-glutamate, an N-terminal fragment of IGF-1 [14]. Veligrotug, an antibody that blocks the IGF-1 receptor, was tested in a phase 3 trial in thyroid eye disease, an autoimmune condition that changes the appearance of the eyes [15].

For recombinant IGF-1 in severe deficiency, a 2009 review in Therapeutics and Clinical Risk Management reported that height velocity rose from about 2.8 cm per year before treatment to about 8 cm per year in the first year, then declined to roughly 4.6 cm per year by year 8 in one American cohort of 76 patients [16]. The review concluded that treatment improves adult height relative to no treatment without achieving normal catch-up, and that most studies were uncontrolled [16]. The same review noted children with GH deficiency grew faster on GH than on IGF-1 [16].

In older adults, trials of exercise and protein supplementation have tracked IGF-1 alongside sarcopenia outcomes: a 2024 meta-analysis of ten randomised trials with 1,154 participants found whey protein supplementation raised appendicular muscle mass index and gait speed [17], and a 2017 trial compared exercise types for body composition, strength and IGF-1 in sarcopenic obesity [18]. A 2024 trial compared two forms of creatine alongside resistance training for effects on anabolic hormones including IGF-1 [19].

Wikipedia reports that high protein intake raises IGF-1, as do dairy (other than cheese) and fish consumption, while calorie restriction showed no effect; oral IGF-1 from milk is largely digested, and the FDA has said IGF-1 in milk is small relative to the body's own levels [1]. Low levels are seen in advanced liver disease and with oral estrogens, which blunt GH-induced IGF-1 production in the liver [1].

A 2017 randomised trial of 100 participants tested a fasting-mimicking diet and measured IGF-1 among markers of ageing and disease risk [20]. Community posts discuss sugar, carbohydrates, chromium and sleep timing as influences on IGF-1; these claims are summarised under Claims and evidence below [4][5][21].

Wikipedia reports that both high and low IGF-1 are associated with higher mortality, with the lowest mortality at mid-range values (about 120 to 160 ng/ml in a 2022 analysis); low levels are linked to type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, while high levels are associated with cancer risk, including colon and thyroid cancer in acromegaly [1]. People with Laron syndrome appear to have lower rates of cancer and type 2 diabetes, and about 100 people studied in a cohort in Ecuador's Loja province reported no diabetes and one cancer [1][8]. A review of IGF-1 signalling in colorectal cancer discusses how the pathway may link high-glycemic diets to tumour glucose metabolism [22].

For mecasermin, the 2009 review listed hypoglycemia in 49 percent of long-term patients (many were hypoglycemic before treatment), thymic hypertrophy in 35 percent, injection-site lipohypertrophy in 32 percent, and tonsil or adenoid enlargement, snoring and reduced hearing in about 22 percent each; antibodies to IGF-1 developed in some, and long-term cancer risk was described as unknown [16].

Mecasermin is prescription-only in the US, Canada and Australia [7]. Growth hormone is available only by prescription in the US and a 1990 federal law made distributing it for non-medical use a felony [23]. IGF-1 and its analogues fall under the peptide hormone and growth factor class that sports bodies prohibit [13].

Looksmax.org hosts many threads on "IGF-1 signaling", mostly in height and facial-bone discussions. Titles include a guide calling it the "key to bone growth", threads about IGF-1 spikes through the day, IGF-1 and the mandible, and a meal thread about growing bones daily [4][5][6][24][25][26]. Other threads concern IGF-1 LR3 and DES, GH peptides for "local IGF-1", where to buy peptides, and adding the GH secretagogue MK-677 to a cycle [27][28][29][30]. One thread argues LR3 is oversold within the peptide industry [31].

On T Nation, IGF-1 comes up in bodybuilding contexts: posts discuss lab ranges on GH, effects of estrogen on IGF-1 and the interaction of insulin and anabolic steroids [32][33][34]. MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an experimental oral ghrelin-receptor agonist that raises GH and IGF-1 and increased lean mass in human studies; it is not approved for sale in the US and is banned in most sports [35].

Human trials examine mecasermin in IGF-1 deficiency [16] and IGF-1 as a marker in exercise, nutrition and sarcopenia trials [17][18][19][20]. A manufacturer-sponsored registry has followed children treated with mecasermin through to adult height. No published trial has tested diet or supplements for raising IGF-1 to increase adult height, and none has tested IGF-1 LR3 for appearance outcomes.

timeline.event: Called the sulfation factor for its effect on cartilage sulfation in vitro; Salmon and Daughaday report the GH-dependent factor in 1957 [1].
Zvi Laron and colleagues describe short children with high GH, later identified as GH-insensitive (Laron syndrome) [8].
Rinderknecht and Humbel publish the amino acid sequence [1].
FDA approves mecasermin products for severe primary IGF-1 deficiency [8].
Analysis reports lowest mortality at mid-range IGF-1 levels [1].
Trofinetide, an analogue of an IGF-1-derived tripeptide, approved in the US for Rett syndrome [14].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, "IGF-1 signaling" threads discuss diet and growth hormone in relation to bone mass, with believers and sceptics arguing over its role; peptide forms and secretagogues are discussed in separate threads [4][5][21].

claims.claim: Supporting IGF-1 signaling through diet (for example avoiding sugar) increases bone mass
claims.believers: Posters say people they know who cut sugar have exceptional bone mass and treat IGF-1 signalling as a route to bone growth; a meal thread describes "growing bones every day" [4][24].
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that IGF-1 contributes to skeletal development and that high protein intake raises levels, while no published trial has tested sugar restriction for adult bone growth [1].

claims.claim: Chromium supplementation raises IGF-1 enough to accelerate bone growth
claims.believers: A poster argues chromium improves insulin sensitivity and collagen production and raises IGF-1 expression, citing animal and cell studies [21].
claims.experts: No published trial has shown that chromium accelerates bone growth in people; the IGF-1 research in the muscle literature concerns signalling mechanisms rather than supplements [3].

claims.claim: Injected IGF-1 forms such as LR3 raise growth for bone and muscle
claims.believers: Threads discuss IGF-1 LR3 and DES as peptides and ask about local effects; others ask about GH peptides for "local IGF-1" [27][28][29].
claims.experts: Approved recombinant IGF-1 (mecasermin) is prescribed for severe deficiency; other forms are not approved products, and mecasermin trials report hypoglycemia as a common adverse event [7][16].

claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread argues LR3 is a heavily marketed peptide that does not live up to its claims [31].
claims.experts: No published human trial has tested IGF-1 LR3 for muscle or bone outcomes in healthy people.

claims.claim: Raising IGF-1 with a secretagogue such as MK-677 supports growth and muscle
claims.believers: Posters discuss adding MK-677 to a cycle for extra IGF-1 [30].
claims.experts: Studies of ibutamoren show raised GH and IGF-1 and increased lean body mass, but it is an investigational drug [35].

claims.claim: Higher IGF-1 is always better for growth and health
claims.believers: Height and bone-growth threads treat high IGF-1 as the goal [25].
claims.experts: Analyses report higher mortality at both low and high IGF-1, with the lowest at mid-range, and high levels are associated with some cancers [1].
